handback.title: Adopter safety: human pull requests pass, audit spares repo checks
handback.summary: An adopter's own pull requests, CI and missing board stop tripping Dokima's checks, audit and card.
handback.feature: Adopters are not tripped on day one. Stories: (1) unplanned pull requests pass; (2) the audit spares repo checks and boards; (3) cards follow CI.

stories.title: Pull requests with no plan pass unless Dokima opened them
stories.user_story: People and Dependabot merge pull requests without a Dokima plan, while Dokima's own stay held to theirs.
stories.context: dokima/checks.py build_matrix returns one failing 'No approved plan found' row for any pull request without an approved plan unless Dokima's app opened it off a try/issue-N branch (manual fix). The Acceptance criteria workflow fails any row with no tests except ids text-only and manual-fix, so a new passing row needs a matching exit there. Add merge.unplanned_prs to dokima/defaults.yaml with allow as the default; any other value (for example block) keeps today's failing check. Dokima's app is agent.BOT.

acceptance_criteria.text: When a person opens a pull request with no approved plan, the Acceptance criteria check passes.
When Dependabot opens a pull request with no approved plan, the Acceptance criteria check passes.
When Dokima opens an issue's pull request with no approved plan, the Acceptance criteria check still fails.
acceptance_criteria.words: only Dokima's own PRs are held to the plan

acceptance_criteria.text: When the unplanned pull requests setting is not allow, a person's unplanned pull request fails the check.

stories.title: The audit spares the repo's checks and a missing board
stories.user_story: The Setup issue no longer flags the repo's own required checks or a missing board.
stories.context: dokima/audit.py compare_rule adds a line for every required check Dokima does not declare (the 'a check Dokima does not declare' list); that list should go. main() exits 1 with an error when DOKIMA_BOARD is empty, check() always reads board fields and views, and run() calls needs_you, which writes to the board. With no board, skip the board reads and the Needs you mark, and still report the other drift: a check Dokima declares that the rule lacks still gets its line.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the branch rule requires a check the repo added, the Setup issue lists no line about it.
acceptance_criteria.words: Checks the repo added are not drift.

acceptance_criteria.text: When no board is set, the audit finishes with exit code 0.
acceptance_criteria.words: The audit fails when no board is set; boards are optional and only exist for organizations.

acceptance_criteria.text: When no board is set, the Setup issue lists no line about board fields or views.
acceptance_criteria.words: No board means nothing to report.

acceptance_criteria.text: When no board is set and the branch rule lacks a check Dokima needs, the Setup issue lists that check.

stories.title: The card follows the repo's own CI
stories.user_story: The card redraws when the repo's own CI finishes, and shows every check the merge needs.
stories.context: The adopter's thin workflow dokima/install/dokima.yml listens to workflow_run only for its own dokima workflow, and entry.yml's card job only for runs started by pull_request_target, merge_group, push and review events, so the repo's own CI finishing never redraws the card. dokima/card.py done_row draws only Dokima's checks (all tests, Acceptance criteria) from the PR head's check runs. The issue explicitly asks for the card change, so dokima/card.py and the workflow files are in scope here.

acceptance_criteria.text: When the repo's own CI finishes on a pull request, its issue's card redraws.
acceptance_criteria.words: The card redraws only when Dokima's own workflows finish, not when the adopter's CI does.

acceptance_criteria.text: The card shows each check the branch rule requires, the repo's own included, with its state.
acceptance_criteria.words: The merge gate already waits on every required check; the card must show them.

answers.why: The owner answered: leave both out, since they already work from the settings file.
Story 2 adds a criterion: with no board, a missing required check is still listed.
